title: Power
notes: **Power definition:** the rate at which work is done. $P = \frac{W}{t}$.
**Alternative form:** since $W = Fs$, $P = Fs/t = Fv$ when force and velocity are in the same direction.
**Units:** SI unit is watt ($1\,\text{W} = 1\,\text{J/s}$). Other units: horsepower ($1\,\text{hp} = 746\,\text{W}$) and kilowatt ($1\,\text{kW} = 1000\,\text{W}$).

**Why $P = Fv$ matters:** it tells you that for a given engine power, a lower speed allows a larger force, and vice versa. This is why cars can climb steep hills in low gear: the engine delivers high force at low wheel speed.
**Average vs instantaneous power:** average power uses total work over total time; instantaneous power uses $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}$ at a specific instant.
